about.title: Personal Injury Help in West Hollywood, California
about.longDescription: West Hollywood is a compact, busy city, and its main corridors carry a lot of daily traffic. Public records show 271 injury collisions in the most recent full year, with 338 people hurt and 2 traffic deaths. Santa Monica Boulevard, Sunset Boulevard, Fountain Avenue, and La Cienega Boulevard are the corridors with the highest recorded collision counts — these are simply the busiest streets by volume, not a judgment about any particular stretch of road. Reported crashes also tend to cluster on Sunday nights into early Monday morning, between roughly midnight and 2 a.m. If you were hurt in a collision, a fall, or another accident anywhere in West Hollywood, LawProactive can help. We're a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney in the area. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your case results in a recovery. There's no obligation to move forward, and reaching out costs nothing. You focus on healing; let someone else look at the legal side.

whyChoose.title: What to Know About Your California Claim

items.title: You Have Time, But Not Forever
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim. If a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to move early.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you share some blame for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means your compensation isn't limited to a fixed dollar amount set by statute.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover money. This lets you get legal help without worrying about hourly rates or retainers.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in West Hollywood?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your claim involves a government agency, such as a city-owned vehicle or property, that deadline can be as short as six months. It's best not to wait to find out which applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partially responsible doesn't prevent you from recovering compensation. Your total recovery is reduced by your share of fault, but you're not shut out entirely.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in West Hollywood?
items.answer: Public collision records show that Santa Monica Boulevard, Sunset Boulevard, Fountain Avenue, and La Cienega Boulevard have the highest recorded crash counts in the city. This simply reflects traffic volume on these busy corridors, not a statement about safety or fault at any particular location.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. California does not cap non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in ordinary personal injury cases. Your potential recovery depends on the facts of your case, not a statutory ceiling.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to LawProactive?
items.answer: No, connecting with an attorney through LawProactive is completely free. We're not a law firm ourselves — we simply connect you with an independent attorney who works on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
